title: What is the sum of the odd numbers from 91 to 109?
description: The odd numbers from ninety one to one hundred nine are added by finding which block of the cube pattern they form. Keeko doubts the sum, because ten squared looks like a fit.
teaching_notes: One idea: the block with n odd numbers adds to n cubed. Watch for students who give n squared instead of n cubed.

video_script.why: The child finds which block of the odd number pattern a long sum forms, and reads its sum as a cube without adding.
video_script.substitution: Count the numbers to find the block number, check where the block starts, then cube the block number.
video_script.anchor: blocks of odd numbers, each block adding to a cube
video_script.wrong_answer: the sum is ten squared, which is one hundred
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies ten by ten and gets one hundred. The pattern gives a cube, so ten is multiplied three times, and ten odd numbers near one hundred must add to far more than one hundred.
video_script.payoff_line: The sum is one thousand, which is ten cubed
maths_rules: 1 = 1³, 3 + 5 = 8 = 2³, 7 + 9 + 11 = 27 = 3³: the block with n odd numbers adds to n³
the first 9 blocks use 1 + 2 + ... + 9 = 45 odd numbers, and the 45th odd number is 89
91 to 109 is ten odd numbers, so it is the 10th block
video_script.design: One idea: the block number gives the cube. Wrong idea: ten odd numbers add to ten squared. The blocks stay in the anchor band and the counting sits on the working board.

<bookmark mark='ten'/>There are ten of them.

beats.on_screen: blocks 1 to 9 use 1 + 2 + ... + 9 = 45 odd numbers; the 45th odd number is 89; so 91 starts the 10th block

marks.nine: the first 9 blocks are marked, using 45 odd numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step two, find which block this is.
<bookmark mark='end'/>The first nine blocks use forty five odd numbers, and the forty fifth odd number is eighty nine.
<bookmark mark='start'/>The next odd number is ninety one, so these ten numbers form the tenth block.
<bookmark mark='cube'/>Step three, use the pattern. The tenth block adds to ten cubed.
<bookmark mark='value'/>Ten times ten times ten is one thousand.

beats.on_screen: check by pairs from the outside: 91 + 109 = 200, 93 + 107 = 200, ... 5 pairs of 200 = 1000

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>Step four, check by pairing the numbers from the outside.
Ninety one plus one hundred nine is two hundred.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Ninety three plus one hundred seven is also two hundred.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Five such pairs make five times two hundred, which is one thousand.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum is one thousand, which is ten cubed.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says 10² = 100; ten odd numbers each near 100 are shown stacked, far taller than 100, and the bubble is struck through; 10 × 10 × 10 appears

marks.big: ten bars, each near 100 tall, are stacked and are far taller than 100
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour and 10 × 10 × 10 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the sum is ten squared, which is one hundred.
<bookmark mark='big'/>But ten odd numbers, each near one hundred, cannot add to only one hundred.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The pattern gives a cube, so ten is multiplied three times.
